title: Finite affine chart factorization and interval gluing
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. There are finite affine open covers $(V_i)$ of $Y$ and $(U_{ij})_j$ of each $f^{-1}(V_i)$ such that the restricted morphism $U_{ij}\to V_i$ factors as a closed immersion $U_{ij}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m_{ij}}_{V_i}$ followed by the smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] separated affine-space projection [def-sbc-affine-space] of relative dimension $m_{ij}\ge0$. All schemes in these factorizations are separated and of finite type over $k$. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Suppose each restriction $K|_{U_{ij}}$ (termwise inverse image along the open immersion [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]) has constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] in an interval $[r_{ij},s_{ij}]$ and Tor amplitude $[a_{ij},b_{ij}]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Then $K$ is bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], with cohomological interval $[\min r_{ij},\max s_{ij}]$ and Tor amplitude $[\min a_{ij},\max b_{ij}]$ if $X$ is nonempty. If $X$ is empty, $K=0$ and every interval is valid.

source.place: Step 7, affine chart factorization and finite-cover gluing of constructibility and Tor intervals.

proof.text: Apply the finite-type definition to the structure map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Since the base is affine, choose finitely many affine opens $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ covering $Y$, with each $R_i$ finitely generated over $k$. Apply the same definition to $f$ over each $V_i$: choose finitely many affine opens $U_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{ij}$ covering $f^{-1}(V_i)$ with $B_{ij}$ finitely generated over $R_i$. The combined family is finite and covers $X$. No claim that $f^{-1}(V_i)$ itself is affine is needed.

source.place: Tag 01T1 (definition-finite-type); finite affine presentation in Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize).

proof.text: For each pair $(i,j)$ choose finitely many $R_i$-algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $B_{ij}$. By the finite-type algebra definition, evaluation $q:R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\twoheadrightarrow B_{ij}$, $t_h\mapsto b_h$, is surjective. Thus $B_{ij}=R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_m]/\ker(q)$, and the affine quotient characterization of closed immersions makes $\operatorname{Spec}(q)$ a closed immersion $U_{ij}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^m_{V_i}$. Its composite with the projection corresponds to the composite $R_i\hookrightarrow R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\xrightarrow{q}B_{ij}$, the original structural ring map. Hence this is the required factorization, with $m=m_{ij}\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 01T0 (section-finite-type), opening paragraph; Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), affine quotient criterion. Affine space over Spec R is Spec R[t_1,...,t_m] as in def-sbc-affine-space.

proof.text: The projection $\mathbf A^{m_{ij}}_{V_i}\to V_i$ is smooth of relative dimension $m_{ij}$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. The source is affine, so this projection is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. The same node applied to the structural maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $V_i$, $U_{ij}$ and $\mathbf A^{m_{ij}}_{V_i}$ are separated over $k$. They are of finite type over $k$: if $r_1,\ldots,r_e$ generate $R_i$ over $k$, then their images together with $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ generate $B_{ij}$ over $k$; and $r_1,\ldots,r_e,t_1,\ldots,t_m$ generate $R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_m]$. The finite-type algebra and affine finite-type definitions give the asserted finite-type structural morphisms. This also covers $m=0$.

proof.text: Finite type over Spec k makes X Noetherian by the Mathlib local-Noetherian and quasi-compactness theorems. This supplies the hypotheses of the proved source open-cover constructibility theorem.

Exact upperStar commutes with homology via mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso. The jointly-surjective family of open inclusions detects zero sheaves by applying conservativity to the zero map F to 0. For a finite index in Type, lift it to Type u only when applying the source conservativity theorem.

Compare finite-constant-value constructibility with IsConstructibleSheaf and apply its existing Noetherian open-cover locality theorem to each homology sheaf. On nonempty X, the finite chart index is nonempty. Take minima of the lower and maxima of the upper endpoints by finite-set extrema. Cohomology vanishes outside these endpoints by the preceding zero test. The enclosing interval [min(rmin,smax),max(rmin,smax)] has ordered endpoints, proving bounded constructibility even for reversed local intervals.

For every module sheaf F, construct the isomorphism between the exact derived pullback of K tensor F[0] and the tensor of the pulled-back K with the pulled-back F in degree zero. Compose leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory, leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso and singleFunctorCompLeftDerivedUpperStarIso. Local Tor vanishing outside the minimum lower and maximum upper endpoints then gives global vanishing by the same homology zero test.

If $X=\varnothing$, every object of its small etale site is empty. The empty family covers each such object, so the sheaf axiom forces every module sheaf to be zero. Every representing complex of $K$ is thus zero, giving $K\cong0$ in the derived category. Its cohomology and the cohomology of its derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf vanish in every degree. The empty stratification gives constructibility. Thus every cohomological and Tor interval is valid; no minimum or maximum of an empty family is formed. Empty charts over a nonempty $X$ are also harmless, since their local vanishing assumptions are vacuous and the displayed minima/maxima still bound all nonempty charts.
